questions.q: How does the summary distinguish Brave New World's dystopia from that of 1984?
a: Its people are enslaved by pleasure rather than pain
Its government rules through constant surveillance
Its citizens are forbidden from taking any drugs
Its society has abandoned science entirely
questions.why: The overview contrasts it with 1984 by noting that pleasure, rather than pain, keeps the citizens captive.

questions.q: How are people created and conditioned in the London of the novel?
a: They are grown in bottles and sleep-taught their caste
They are raised in family homes by trained parents
They are chosen by lottery from the general public
They are cloned from a single ruling family
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes humans grown in bottles as Alphas through Epsilons and conditioned from birth to accept their caste and consume.

questions.q: What role does soma play in the society described?
a: It is a drug that keeps everyone content
It is a test used to assign people to castes
It is a medicine that restores painful emotions
It is a ritual performed at Solidarity Service
questions.why: Lesson 1 calls soma the perfect drug, one of the easy pleasures people are conditioned to prioritize over meaning.

questions.q: According to the summary, what is the main source of suffering for the novel's main characters?
a: Feeling that they do not fit in with their group
Having too little access to soma and comfort
Being forced to read Shakespeare in school
Fearing that their caste will be abolished
questions.why: Lesson 2 says every main character is somehow different from the group they should fit into, and this is their worst suffering.

questions.q: What does John the Savage mean when he claims the right to be unhappy?
a: Genuine happiness requires the possibility of suffering
Misery is always preferable to any comfort
People should reject all forms of community
Unhappiness proves that a society is stable
questions.why: Lesson 3 argues that manufactured contentment is hollow, and that rejecting suffering also rejects deep, real happiness.
